messages:
customer-sre: heads up — after yesterday's private-vpc cert rotation (04:10 UTC) our internal service calls to Redwood endpoints started getting TLS errors and mTLS failures. first seen ~04:12 UTC, ~30% of calls 403/handshake failed.
elaine: sorry about that — are these Dedicated or Private (VPC) endpoints? rough count of failing clients?
customer-sre: Private (VPC). only our internal clients using client certs. non-mTLS requests succeed. ~3 of 10 app instances reporting handshake errors in logs.
matt: can you paste a brief client-side OpenSSL s_client trace (sanitized)? e.g. `openssl s_client -connect <host>:443 -cert client.pem -key client.key -CAfile ca.pem -showcerts`
customer-sre: paste: ```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = Example CA, CN = Example Root CA
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
SSL handshake has read 2302 bytes and written 1483 bytes
---
no peer certificate available
---
```
elaine: that `unable to get local issuer certificate` suggests the gateway rejected client cert chain because the client CA truststore doesn't include the intermediate that the client presented — did you recently update your client CA bundle?
customer-sre: we did an internal CA rotation Friday; clients still present the old chain (cross-signed intermediate). we flipped a configmap for `client-ca-bundle` yesterday too, but not across all gateways?
matt: thanks — two suspicious failure modes we see in private deployments: 1) rotator updated server cert chain but a separate process is responsible for syncing `client-ca-bundle` to the ingress pods; if that sync key was renamed, some pods keep old truststore. 2) a proxy (customer side) could be stripping intermediates. can you run this on a failing pod: `kubectl exec -c gateway <pod> -- ls -l /etc/ssl/client-ca && cat /etc/ssl/client-ca | head -n 40` and paste (redact actual certs)?
customer-sre: ran it on pod gateway-5: `ls -l` shows `/etc/ssl/client-ca -> /etc/configmaps/client-ca-old` (surprising) and file contains only root, no intermediate.
elaine: that confirms; some pods still mounted the old configmap. were there any recent gateway restarts after you updated the configmap? a configmap update doesn't force a restart — only new pods get new mounts.
customer-sre: we updated the configmap but did a rolling restart of gateways — but seemed to hang for a bit during deploy and some pods didn't recreate.
matt: workaround: rotate the client CA mount by forcing a restart of all gateway pods (kubectl rollout restart deploy/gateway). that will ensure all pods pick up `/etc/configmaps/client-ca-new` which contains the intermediate. we can also temporarily allow AIA fetching on the ingress, but in your env egress is blocked so clients can't fetch missing intermediates.
customer-sre: we tried `rollout restart` and failing pods decreased to 0 over 2 minutes — calls resumed. thanks.
elaine: root cause appears to be partial configmap propagation (some pods still pointed to `client-ca-old`). I'll open an ops ticket to check why the deploy hung and why the rotator didn't trigger full rollout.
rotator-bot: auto-alert: rotator sync job finished at 04:09 UTC with status=success; changed keys: server-cert, server-chain. did NOT update `client-ca-bundle` key (no diff detected).
sre-bot: flagged for eng-runtime — suspected missing sync between cert rotator and client-ca sync recipes when customer-managed client CAs are present.
ops: will follow up on why `kubectl rollout restart` was required — configmap update should have been accompanied by CI deploy job.
customer-sre: big thanks — can we get a postmortem note about making client-ca sync atomic with server rotations? we almost had payment timeouts due to the 403s.
elaine: yes — we'll coordinate with eng-runtime and add a recommended playbook: 1) ensure client-ca-bundle is updated and mounted, 2) force restart of gateway pods, 3) verify with `openssl s_client` from inside VPC. we'll also propose a rotator enhancement to detect mismatched client CA mounts. :thumbsup:
